title: Prospective prediction of human efficacy, dose, and major toxicity before first-in-human exposure

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a model, a human experimental system, or a combination of the two that can predict how a previously undosed drug will perform in people before anyone receives it. Its predictions would jointly specify whether the drug produces a clinically meaningful effect, the dose regimen needed to produce that effect, and the risk of specified major toxicities. Those predictions would be fixed in advance and subsequently checked against human trials.

Quantitative systems pharmacology, machine learning and physiologically based pharmacokinetics already contribute to drug development. The proposed advance would connect their component predictions to clinically confirmed outcomes. Predicting drug exposure alone does not establish efficacy or safety, and fitting a model to completed trials does not demonstrate that it could have predicted those trials beforehand. The 2025 modeling review supports the importance of testing models against new evidence, while describing confident efficacy and toxicity prediction as a continuing challenge.

significance.text: Reliable foresight about clinical drug action before first-in-human dosing would materially change how drugs are selected and developed. Developers could use predicted efficacy, dose and serious-toxicity risk together when deciding which candidates deserve clinical testing. The 2025 modeling review identifies substantial potential for predictive methods to improve development decisions and reduce late-stage failures. Achieving this prospectively across unrelated diseases would turn more of pharmacology into a science of advance prediction.

Reduced attrition is a plausible consequence, but its magnitude would depend on deployment and on which failures the method can anticipate. Clinical development success also depends on trial design and execution, regulatory decisions and company strategy. Consequently, the low historical probability of reaching approval cannot be interpreted as the fraction of failures that a biological predictor would prevent. Any claim that the method reduces overall attrition would require its own evidence from use in development programs.

Scope synthesis: predicting an average treatment effect in a defined trial population would not by itself identify which individual patients will benefit. Manufacturing, regulatory acceptance and harms too rare for adequate pre-market assessment would remain separate problems. Faster molecular screening could help supply candidates, but it would demonstrate a narrower capability than confirmed prediction of their clinical outcomes. No greater-than-95-percent accuracy target or greater-than-50-percent attrition reduction is adopted here; the supplied material does not establish either threshold.

missing_breakthrough.text: The central scientific barrier is linking molecular action to effects that emerge across cells, organs and whole people. A binding constant alone does not determine whether an organ changes function, a patient improves or a trial meets its endpoint. The 2025 review describes efficacy and toxicity as emergent properties of interactions across biological scales and identifies variation among individuals as another obstacle. A successful method would need to capture enough of these interactions to predict both beneficial and harmful effects under a specified dosing regimen.

Engineering synthesis: the missing capability is dependable joint prediction under conditions that prevent hindsight from substituting for foresight. The method must connect dose and exposure to clinical response, express uncertainty, and retain useful performance on compounds and disease mechanisms outside its development data. A human experimental system is an alternative route to this target, but the supplied review does not directly assess how close such systems are to meeting the full requirement.

Scope synthesis: major toxicity must be defined through named outcomes, relevant exposures, follow-up periods and assessable risk thresholds. A prediction that no toxicity will ever occur cannot be confirmed by a finite trial. Idiosyncratic immune-mediated injury is assigned to PHA-03 as an editorial boundary, and is excluded from the proposed PHA-02 demonstration. The supplied evidence does not establish the earlier rationale that this category is uniformly human-specific and rare.

current_state.text: Zhou and colleagues’ study, published on 29 October 2025, reconstructed 20,398 clinical development programs spanning 2001–2023. It reports that published estimates of clinical success have ranged from about 7 to 20 percent, with differences in datasets, methods and time periods limiting direct comparison. Its Table 3 gives an adjusted Phase 1-to-approval overall success rate of 7.2 percent for small-molecule programs in the 2015–2023 window. This is a development-success statistic, not a measure of predictor accuracy or the proportion of failures preventable through better pharmacology.

The supplied review reports that the relevant methods and Table 3 were available in the extracted main paper, although the retained HTML and PDF text truncate later during the references. Some supplementary PDFs also have extraction limitations, including pages without extractable text. Those limitations do not invalidate the reviewed table, but the supplementary files are not used here to infer additional findings.

Grace Zhang and Tongli Zhang’s review, published on 9 August 2025, describes established modeling approaches and concludes that their predictive potential remains incompletely realized. The supplied evidence review had the complete seven-page article and found support for both the continuing efficacy/toxicity challenge and its multiscale explanation. This is an assessment of modeling practice and its barriers; it is not a direct prospective test of the joint capability proposed here.

Bender and colleagues’ 2026 perspective on artificial intelligence in drug discovery describes evidence of clinically relevant impact as limited. It was published online on 7 August 2026, so its November issue date does not place it beyond the 1 November 2026 assessment date. Only the PubMed record and abstract were available to the supplied review. That abstract supports the attributed assessment, but cannot establish the article’s full reasoning or the worldwide absence of a prospectively validated joint predictor.

The supplied FDA overview of new approach methodologies describes efforts to improve the human relevance of nonclinical testing, reduce or replace animal use, and validate or qualify methods for particular purposes. The reviewed overview does not present clinical confirmation of joint pre-human predictions of efficacy, dose and major toxicity. Its broad prediction ambitions should therefore be distinguished from a demonstrated result meeting this proposal. The overview was available in full, but its linked guidance and reports were not supplied or inspected in the review.

Evidence-bound synthesis: the supplied sources document substantial development attrition, existing predictive tools and continuing scientific challenges. They do not directly demonstrate the proposed capability, and they also do not prove that no method meeting it exists anywhere. No bounded freshness-search record was supplied, so a literature-wide conclusion about achievement as of 1 November 2026 remains unresolved.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: select compounds that have never been administered to humans and were excluded from method training. Before first-in-human dosing, lock the method, its inputs and its predictions. For each compound, specify the target population, dose regimen, primary clinical endpoint, predicted direction and approximate size of the effect, and the predicted risk of a named serious toxicity at defined exposure and follow-up. Retrospective agreement with completed trials would not satisfy this prospective requirement.
completion_criteria.label: Lock predictions for training-excluded compounds before first-in-human dosing

completion_criteria.text: Proposed assessment rules: establish numerical acceptance tolerances for dose and effect predictions, uncertainty bounds, validation sample sizes and criteria for assessing toxicity risk before outcomes become known. Count every prospectively evaluated compound, including failed predictions and discontinued programs, and explain missing or unevaluable outcomes. An absence-of-toxicity prediction should mean that risk lies below a predefined, statistically assessable threshold; observing no events cannot establish zero risk.
completion_criteria.label: Predefine numerical acceptance tolerances and account for every evaluated compound

completion_criteria.text: Proposed breadth and reproducibility: confirm performance in clinical trials across at least three mechanistically unrelated indications, then seek independent replication using new compounds and a reproducible version of the method or experimental procedure. Three indications is a proposed benchmark rather than an established scientific or regulatory standard. Even successful results would establish the demonstrated breadth of prediction, not literal universality across drugs, diseases or populations.
completion_criteria.label: Confirm performance across three mechanistically unrelated indications; seek independent replication

completion_criteria.text: Proposed practical boundaries: report where the method is applicable, where uncertainty is too large for a useful decision, and which populations, exposure ranges, follow-up durations and toxicity classes remain untested. Idiosyncratic immune-mediated injury assigned to PHA-03 is outside this demonstration. Claims of individual benefit prediction or reduced development attrition would require additional validation beyond agreement with average clinical effects, efficacious dose and the specified toxicity risks.
completion_criteria.label: Report applicability limits, untested scope, and claims requiring additional validation

related_concepts.text: Roster-based scope synthesis: PHA-03, general prevention of idiosyncratic immune-mediated drug injury, addresses a particular class of harm that PHA-02 explicitly leaves outside its proposed demonstration. Prediction and prevention remain different achievements: anticipating a harmful response does not itself prevent it. PHA-04, antigen-chosen pharmacological control of immune memory, concerns deliberate alteration of immune function rather than forecasting clinical outcomes; its interventions could eventually become subjects for PHA-02 validation.

Roster-based scope synthesis: PHA-01 concerns designing pharmacological control of proteins without usable binding pockets; PHA-05 concerns systemic access to brain parenchyma across drug classes; and PHA-11 concerns reliable oral systemic exposure for folded peptides and proteins. These are advances in target control or delivery. They could enable new candidates and supply information relevant to prediction, but successful binding, tissue access or systemic exposure alone would not establish human clinical efficacy and major-toxicity prediction.

Roster-based scope synthesis: PHA-06 concerns replacing missing human cell types in place, PHA-07 dismantling pathogenic protein conformations while restoring function, and PHA-12 triggering scarless regrowth of complex adult mammalian structures. Each seeks a specific therapeutic capability. PHA-02 would instead seek to forecast the clinical effects, useful doses and specified serious risks of drugs pursuing those capabilities. Creating a therapy and predicting its performance remain separate achievements.

Roster-based scope synthesis: PHA-08 targets eradication of dormant infectious persisters without seeding genetic resistance, while PHA-09 targets a change in human aging rate across organ systems. Their outcomes could become demanding prediction targets for PHA-02, but neither would be established merely by showing that a prediction method works in other indications. Conversely, development of one such therapy would not demonstrate predictive generalization across unrelated diseases.

Roster-based scope synthesis: PHA-10 seeks severe analgesia uncoupled from respiratory depression and reinforcement, making it closely related to PHA-02’s concern with benefit and harm at a useful dose. It remains a particular therapeutic achievement rather than a general prediction method. PHA-13 seeks a medicine that maintains its own therapeutic window without an external controller. Such self-regulation would alter how exposure and effect are controlled during treatment; PHA-02 concerns advance prediction of their clinical consequences.

change_log.change: Preserved PHA-02’s identity while defining the innovation as a proposed joint prospective capability.
change_log.reason: The evidence documents a substantial prediction challenge but does not establish universal absence of a qualifying method.

change_log.change: Integrated the multiscale explanation and inter-individual variability into the scientific barriers.
change_log.reason: These supported distinctions explain why molecular measurements alone cannot determine clinical outcomes.

change_log.change: Replaced individual-benefit implications and guaranteed attrition reduction with bounded, conditional consequences.
change_log.reason: Trial-average prediction does not establish individual response prediction, and development failures have biological and nonbiological causes.

change_log.change: Specified the 7.2 percent result as adjusted small-molecule Phase 1-to-approval success for 2015–2023 within a reconstruction of 20,398 programs.
change_log.reason: The denominator, time window and adjustment prevent confusion with predictor accuracy or preventable failure rates.

change_log.change: Preserved source-specific access limits, the 2026 perspective’s online publication date and the limited scope of the FDA observation.
change_log.reason: Abstract-only access, extraction truncation and unreviewed linked documents constrain interpretation without disproving the reported findings.

change_log.change: Expanded completion criteria to include locked methods, defined populations and endpoints, tolerances, uncertainty, complete accounting and assessable toxicity thresholds.
change_log.reason: These proposed rules make confirmation interpretable, discourage selective reporting and avoid treating zero observed events as zero risk.

change_log.change: Made independent reproducibility and finite demonstrated breadth explicit while retaining three unrelated indications as a proposal.
change_log.reason: A convincing demonstration needs reproducibility, but neither a finite test set nor the proposed indication count establishes universality.

change_log.change: Retained PHA-03 as a scope separation and removed the unsupported biological rationale for that separation.
change_log.reason: The supplied evidence does not substantiate the general human-specificity and rarity characterization.

change_log.change: Explained overlap and distinctions with every other supplied roster entry without merging them.
change_log.reason: Target control, delivery, therapeutic action, harm prevention and self-regulation remain distinct from prospective clinical prediction.

change_log.change: Did not adopt historical accuracy or attrition-reduction thresholds.
change_log.reason: The historical comparison list was not supplied, and the evidence does not establish those numerical targets.

unresolved_issues: Whether any method already meets the full prospective joint-prediction target remains unresolved; no bounded freshness-search record was supplied.
The supplied review does not directly assess the current capabilities and limitations of human experimental systems as an alternative route to the target.
An executable validation protocol still needs numerical dose and effect tolerances, uncertainty requirements, compound counts, sample sizes, toxicity thresholds and rules for unevaluable outcomes.
The precise boundary between PHA-02 major toxicities and PHA-03 idiosyncratic immune-mediated injury needs operational definitions.
The effect of deploying a successful predictor on overall development attrition, cost or timelines would require separate evidence.
The historical comparison list and the provenance of its numerical thresholds remain unavailable; no claim that those figures were definitively disproved or exhaustively traced is made.
The 2026 AI perspective is represented only by its abstract, and the FDA overview’s linked documents were not reviewed. These limits leave broader conclusions about those materials unresolved.
